blueprint.name: Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech)
blueprint.source: JEE Main Paper 1: 75 questions, 300 marks, 180 minutes; 25 per subject (20 MCQ + 5 numerical); +4/-1.

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr magnetons) of the complex ion [CoF₆]³⁻ is closest to:
questions.solution: Shortcut: F⁻ is a weak field ligand, so Co(III) (d⁶) is high‑spin with 4 unpaired electrons; μ = √[4(6)] ≈ 4.90 BM. Full solution: Co(III) is d⁶; in octahedral high‑spin configuration t₂g⁴ e_g² gives 4 unpaired electrons; spin‑only formula μ = √[n(n+2)] yields √24 = 4.90 BM.

questions.text: The length of the focal chord of the parabola y² = 8x inclined at an angle of 60° with the positive x-axis is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Length of focal chord of y²=4ax with slope m is 4a(1+m²)/m². Here 4a=8 ⇒ a=2, m=tan60°=√3. Length = 8(1+3)/3 = 32/3. Full: Focus is (2,0). Line with slope √3: y=√3(x-2). Intersect with y²=8x ⇒ 3(x-2)²=8x ⇒ 3x²-20x+12=0. Distance between roots = √(1+m²)|x₁-x₂| = 2√[(20/3)²-16] = 2√(256/9) = 32/3.

questions.text: A particle is moving with velocity v = 2t² + 3t. Find its acceleration at t = 2s.

A satellite of mass m is in a circular orbit around Earth (mass M, radius R) at a height h = R above the surface. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the satellite to the magnitude of its gravitational potential energy is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For any bound circular orbit, the Virial Theorem gives K = -E_total and |U| = 2K, so K/|U| = 1/2 directly. Full Solution: Orbital radius r = 2R. Velocity v² = GM/r. Kinetic Energy K = ½mv² = GMm/2r. Potential Energy U = -GMm/r. Magnitude |U| = GMm/r. Ratio K/|U| = (GMm/2r) / (GMm/r) = 1/2.

questions.text: Which of the following alkyl chlorides undergoes an SN1 reaction most readily?
questions.solution: Shortcut: SN1 rate depends on carbocation stability; tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl, so (CH₃)₃CCl (tert‑butyl chloride) reacts fastest. Full solution: SN1 proceeds via carbocation formation; the tert‑butyl cation is stabilized by three electron‑donating methyl groups, making its formation easiest among the given options.

questions.text: The bond order of the peroxide ion (O₂²⁻) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: O₂²⁻ is isoelectronic with F₂ (18 electrons), which has a bond order of 1. Full solution: O₂ has 16 electrons with bond order 2. Adding two electrons to O₂ fills the antibonding π* orbitals, giving 10 bonding and 8 antibonding electrons; bond order = (10 – 8)/2 = 1.

questions.text: There are 10 points in a plane, no three of which are collinear except 4 points which are collinear. The number of triangles that can be formed by joining these points is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total triangles from 10 points = ¹⁰C₃ = 120. Triangles lost due to 4 collinear points = ⁴C₃ = 4. Required triangles = 120 - 4 = 116. Full Solution: Select any 3 points out of 10 to form a triangle in ¹⁰C₃ ways. However, any 3 points chosen from the 4 collinear points do not form a triangle. Subtract these ⁴C₃ invalid cases. ¹⁰C₃ - ⁴C₃ = 120 - 4 = 116.
questions.topic: Permutations and Combinations (Combinations with Collinear Points)

questions.text: The packing efficiency of a body‑centered cubic (BCC) unit cell is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Memorize standard packing efficiencies: simple cubic 52%, BCC 68%, FCC 74%. Full solution: In BCC, atoms touch along body diagonal; volume occupied = 2 × (4/3)πr³, cell volume = (4r/√3)³; packing fraction = √3π/8 ≈ 0.68 = 68%.

questions.text: The sum of the infinite series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n(n+1)(n+2)}$ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Write the general term as $\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{n(n+1)}-\frac{1}{(n+1)(n+2)}\right]$; the series telescopes to $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{1\cdot2}=\frac{1}{4}$. Full solution: Using partial fractions, $\frac{1}{n(n+1)(n+2)}=\frac{1}{2n}-\frac{1}{n+1}+\frac{1}{2(n+2)}$; summing from $n=1$ to $N$ and taking $N\to\infty$ gives $\frac{1}{4}$.

questions.text: In a photoelectric experiment, light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a metal surface. If the work function of the metal is φ, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation K_max = hν - φ. Since ν = 1.5 ν₀ and φ = hν₀, K_max = 1.5φ - φ = 0.5φ. Full solution: The threshold frequency ν₀ satisfies φ = hν₀. Incident frequency ν = 1.5ν₀ gives photon energy hν = 1.5hν₀ = 1.5φ. Subtracting work function yields K_max = 1.5φ - φ = 0.5φ.

questions.text: If the mean and variance of a binomial distribution are 4 and 2 respectively, then P(X = 1) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For Binomial, Mean=np=4, Variance=npq=2 ⇒ q=1/2, p=1/2, n=8. P(X=1) = ⁿC₁ p qⁿ⁻¹ = 8 × (1/2) × (1/2)⁷ = 8/256 = 1/32. Full: Given np=4 and np(1-p)=2. Dividing gives 1-p=1/2 ⇒ p=1/2. Then n=8. P(X=1) = 8 × (1/2)¹ × (1/2)⁷ = 1/32.

questions.text: A convex lens has focal length 20 cm. At what distance from the lens should an object be placed to get a real image twice the size of object?
questions.solution: Magnification m = -2 (real image). m = v/u = -2 ⇒ v = -2u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. 1/20 = 1/(-2u) - 1/u = -3/(2u). u = -30 cm. So object distance = 30 cm.

questions.text: The escape velocity of a body from Earth is 11.2 km/s. What is the escape velocity from a planet having mass 4 times and radius twice that of Earth?
questions.solution: v_e = v(2GM/R). For new planet: v_e' = v(2G·4M/2R) = v(2·2GM/R) = v2·v(2GM/R) = v2 × 11.2 = 15.84 km/s.

questions.text: The standard Gibbs free energy change for a reaction at 298 K is –11.4 kJ mol⁻¹. The equilibrium constant K at this temperature is closest to:
questions.solution: Shortcut: At 298 K, RT ≈ 2.48 kJ mol⁻¹; –ΔG°/RT = 11.4/2.48 ≈ 4.6, so ln K ≈ 4.6 → K ≈ e⁴·⁶ ≈ 100. Full solution: ΔG° = –RT ln K → ln K = –ΔG°/(RT) = 11400 J / (8.314×298) ≈ 4.60 → K = e⁴·⁶⁰ ≈ 99.5 ≈ 100.

questions.text: The value of the definite integral ∫₀^{π/2} (sin³x)/(sin³x + cos³x) dx is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use King's Property: I = ∫₀^{π/2} f(sin x, cos x) dx = ∫₀^{π/2} f(cos x, sin x) dx. Let I be the given integral. Replacing x by π/2 - x gives I = ∫₀^{π/2} (cos³x)/(cos³x + sin³x) dx. Adding the two expressions: 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} 1 dx = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4. Full Solution: Let I = ∫₀^{π/2} sin³x/(sin³x+cos³x) dx. Substitute x → π/2 - x: I = ∫₀^{π/2} cos³x/(sin³x+cos³x) dx. Adding: 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} (sin³x+cos³x)/(sin³x+cos³x) dx = ∫₀^{π/2} dx = π/2. Therefore, I = π/4.
